features.name: impression_log_norm
features.description: Log-scaled exposure count normalized by training-fold minimum and maximum; compresses rare extreme counts while retaining exposure intensity.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a smooth exposure-intensity coordinate for a linear SVM margin with reduced influence from very large counts.

features.name: impression_tail_intensity
features.description: Smooth high-exposure tail severity relative to the training-fold average impression count; values near zero indicate ordinary or below-average exposure.
features.expected_model_benefit: Gives the margin a separate slope for very repeated exposures without requiring a nonlinear transform inside the model.

features.name: slot_visibility_score
features.description: Weighted page-slot visibility estimate from position and depth, with top, shallow placements scored higher and lower, deeper placements scored lower.
features.expected_model_benefit: Combines display position and page depth into one approximate attention direction suitable for a linear weight.

features.name: relative_slot_position_norm
features.description: Normalized bottomness of the shown position within the available depth; zero corresponds to the first slot or a single-slot page and one corresponds to the bottom of a multi-slot page.
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures relative slot ordering so lower placements can be separated from top placements along a single axis.

features.name: ad_id_band_norm
features.description: Ad identifier location within the training-fold numeric range, clipped to keep future out-of-range values bounded.
features.expected_model_benefit: Keeps ad namespace effects as bounded numeric variation rather than raw large identifiers.

features.name: advertiser_id_band_norm
features.description: Advertiser identifier location within the training-fold numeric range, representing broad campaign-owner namespace bands.
features.expected_model_benefit: Adds a bounded advertiser coordinate that a linear SVM can weight without instability from raw identifier scale.

features.name: ad_advertiser_band_gap
features.description: Absolute separation between normalized ad and advertiser identifier bands, measuring cross-entity namespace alignment.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a simple cross-entity consistency coordinate for campaigns where ad and advertiser namespaces move together.

features.name: creative_completeness_score
features.description: Share of keyword, title, and description identifiers that are nonzero, treating zero as a sparse metadata marker.
features.expected_model_benefit: Lets the margin react to sparse versus complete creative metadata using a continuous score.

features.name: content_id_log_centroid
features.description: Average of log-normalized keyword, title, and description identifier magnitudes, using training-fold maxima for scaling.
features.expected_model_benefit: Condenses multiple content identifiers into one bounded projection, reducing scale imbalance for SVM optimization.

features.name: user_id_log_norm
features.description: Log-normalized user identifier magnitude; zero-coded users remain at the bottom of the scale.
features.expected_model_benefit: Represents user identity granularity with compression of huge id values and a natural zero point for unknown users.

features.name: display_attention_judgment
features.description: A 0.0-to-1.0 assessor score of how much attention the displayed item is likely to receive from its row-level layout signals, especially depth, position, and exposure count.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides an additional attention prior that can align with formula slot features while remaining robust to unusual page configurations.

features.name: creative_trace_quality_judgment
features.description: A 0.0-to-1.0 assessor score reflecting whether keyword, title, and description identifiers look like a complete, coherent creative trace rather than sparse or placeholder metadata.
features.expected_model_benefit: Adds a semantic quality score for metadata completeness and consistency, complementing exact zero checks and log scales.
